# MIRA's Find Positions of Interest Tool

The **find_positions_of_interest** workflow is a utility tool that runs DAIS-ribosome and reports all amino acid and nucleotide alleles at positions specified in your positions of interest table. Unlike the main MIRA pipeline, this workflow allows you to rerun the analysis on different sets of samples or positions without processing raw sequencing data.

To get started, you'll need to provide query sequences in FASTA format, a reference sequence FASTA file, a variants table, and a positions of interest table. Once complete, you'll get a CSV file that lists all codon and amino acid information at the specified positions, regardless of whether they differ from the reference sequence. Check out the info below for more details about how it works.

![find_positions_of_int workflow](../../docs/images/find_variants_of_interst_workflow_img_v3.png)
_find_positions_of_int workflow_

### The Query Sequences Input

The input file for this workflow is a FASTA file containing assembled sequences from your samples. If you've run the MIRA pipeline, you'll find this input file named `DAIS_ribosome_input.fasta` in the dais-ribosome folder within the aggregate outputs. You can also provide any other assembled sequences in FASTA format.

### The Reference Sequence File

The reference sequence file should contain the reference sequences in FASTA format thaty ou would like to compare your query seqeunces with. These will be used by DAIS-ribosome to align with and compare against your query sequences.
```
>PHUKET3073_B_HA_68235

>PHUKET3073_B_MP_68238

>PHUKET3073_B_NA_68234

>PHUKET3073_B_NP_71049

>BRISBANE60_B_NS_115367

>PHUKET3073_B_NS_68237

>PHUKET3073_B_PA_68233

>PHUKET3073_B_PB1_68239

>PHUKET3073_B_PB2_68232


```

### The Variants Table Input

The variants table should contain variant information and can be generated from your analysis. This table is used in conjunction with the positions of interest to filter and report the relevant alleles. The file format should match the output from your variant calling analysis.

```
subtype	protein	positions	amino_acid
H1N1	NA	275	Y
ALL	PA	38	F
ALL	PA	38	M
H3N2	NA	119	V
H3N2	NA	292	K
BVIC	NA	197	N
BVIC	HA-signal	2	S
BVIC	HA	200	S

```

# Input Parameters for find_positions_of_interest Workflow

| Flag                    | Description                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `profile`               | singularity, docker, local, sge, slurm. You can use docker or singularity. Use local for running on local computer. |
| `outdir`                | The file path to where you would like the output directory to write the files. The full file path is required.      |
| `positions_of_interest` | (required) The file path to your `positions_of_interest.txt` file with the format described above. The full file path is required. |
| `reference_seq_fasta`   | (required) The file path to your reference sequences FASTA file. The full file path is required.                   |
| `variants_table`        | (required) The file path to your variants table file. The full file path is required.                              |

### Optional Parameters

| Flag        | Description                                                                                              |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `process_q` | (optional, required for HPC profiles) Provide the name of the processing queue that will submit to the queue. |
| `email`     | (optional) Provide an email if you would like to receive an email notification upon completion.         |

### Running the Workflow

To run the find_positions_of_interest workflow, use the command below:

```bash
nextflow run ./main.nf \
   -profile <profile> \
   --outdir <OUTDIR> \
   --positions_of_interest <filepath>/positions_of_interest.txt \
   --reference_seq_fasta <filepath>/reference_sequences.fasta \
   --variants_table <filepath>/variants_table.txt \
   --process_q <QUEUE_NAME> \
   --email <EMAIL_ADDRESS> (optional)
```

**Parameters:**
- `<profile>`: The execution profile (docker, singularity, local, slurm, sge, etc.)
- `<OUTDIR>`: The output directory path where results will be written
- `<filepath>/positions_of_interest.txt`: Full path to your positions of interest file
- `<filepath>/reference_sequences.fasta`: Full path to your reference sequences FASTA file
- `<filepath>/variants_table.txt`: Full path to your variants table file
- `<QUEUE_NAME>`: (HPC only) The queue name for job submission
- `<EMAIL_ADDRESS>`: (Optional) Your email for completion notification
